stationMultiplayerConfigure.when: After System.loadLibrary and before NativeActivity super.onCreate; signed immutable launch only.
stationMultiplayerConfigure.reject: Invalid slot/mask/count or a native Activity already owns the runtime.

stationMultiplayerBind.when: Host only, after NativeActivity creation and Socket.bind(127.0.0.1, 0), before connect to the native host. Each guest has its own persistent local TCP socket.
stationMultiplayerBind.reject: Duplicate slot/port, local slot, slot outside signed mask, missing staged launch or more than three bindings.

stationMultiplayerUnbind.when: Only release an unclaimed reservation after a failed initial local connect. Accepted native TCP sockets retain the mapping across WSS epochs.
stationMultiplayerUnbind.reject: Reservation already claimed by a native accepted fd or wrong port/slot.

controllerRequirements.slots: Zero-based controller ports 0..3, not native client indices or TCP accept order.
controllerRequirements.mask: Exactly participantCount distinct bits within 0x0f, including localSlot; count 2..4.
controllerRequirements.configuration: Each participant requests only its signed controller bit; no sharing or slave flag. Android touch remains on the first local pad; upstream maps it to the requested network device.
controllerRequirements.coreProfile: Java must configure the same qualified per-title input profile on all peers, including a corrected SNES multitap core where required. This runtime alone does not make a two-player title support four players.

recoveryRequirements.oneCoordinator: Java aggregates every channel and peer against one room epoch before issuing native resume.
recoveryRequirements.quorum: Native self PLAYING; connected_players client bitmap and client_devices union exactly equal the signed roster; host each active fd maps to its signed slot; guest has the host connection active.
recoveryRequirements.drain: Every active native send buffer is flushed and empty before ready is returned. Java still owns relay ACK/replay/credit and collective barrier.
recoveryRequirements.staleConfirmation: V3 captures a native request revision before polling; a concurrent epoch, wait or visibility change rejects confirmation from the earlier request.
recoveryRequirements.lifecycle: Configure is consumed once at NativeActivity creation. Only final owner release after thread join clears it. Android onStop and WSS reconnect do not clear it.
recoveryRequirements.allocationFailure: Accepted source port is claimed only after both native socket buffers are allocated. A failure consumes no signed slot and reports native recovery failure in v3. Rejected claims release both buffers before closing the incoming fd.
recoveryRequirements.v2: Original two-player readiness predicate, protocol bytes, timers and latency presets remain unchanged. Runtime identity still changes: never reuse the rs4 runtime hash for this new binary.

validationScope.nativeTests: Production C header and readiness/poll/peer-validation functions extracted into a Windows harness with real mutexes and 64 real concurrent epoch changes; RetroArch arrays, sync/flush and getpeername are fixtures.
validationScope.reproducibility: Historical baseline __DATE__ is pinned through SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1791331200. Candidate uses 1791417600. The baseline differs from R74 only in the 20-byte GNU build-id descriptor at file offset 736. Every other file byte is identical, including all code/data/layout/relocations. Candidate build independently recomputes that bounded comparison and refuses any other difference. Whole-file identity is not claimed; no build-id was patched. See baseline-comparison.json.
